headline: Take-Two Interactive got hammered last night while oil cratered 5%, but the ASX held up relatively well today — and Google just dropped a major new AI model called Gemini Omni.

portfolio.summary: A quiet day on the ASX for your local holdings, with everything barely moving. The action was really last night on the US side — Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) was the big story, dropping 4.4%. GOOGL also slipped 1.2%. Your ASX-listed ETFs (VDHG, VGE, VTS, FUEL) all closed within a fraction of their previous prices, which is pretty much a non-event.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Big drop last night — down 4.4% to $227.55. No specific earnings catalyst in the data, but GTA 6 collector's edition pre-order news is circulating, suggesting hype is building ahead of release. The drop may reflect broader market nerves or profit-taking after a strong run.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Down 1.2% to $382.97 last night despite recent strong earnings. Google did just drop a major new AI model called Gemini Omni today — that could be a positive catalyst when US markets open tonight.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: Down 0.9% at today's ASX close to $8.78. Oil (WTI crude) cratered 5% last night to $91.76 — that's the real pressure point here. OPEC also cut its global oil demand growth forecast for 2026, which isn't helping sentiment for energy stocks.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: The one bright spot today — up 0.26% to $92.62 at the ASX close. The Aussie dollar ticking up slightly (now 71.7 US cents) can sometimes help emerging market ETFs priced in AUD.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: Edged down 0.32% to $515.43 at today's close, tracking the mild softness in US markets from last night's session.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Essentially flat last night — down just 0.12% to $418.57. AI and cloud momentum continues to be the narrative, with analysts watching whether revenue growth can keep pace with the AI hype.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ finished slightly positive — the S&P up 0.37% and the NASDAQ up 0.19%. The ASX 200 closed today down 0.42% at 8,655. The big mover was crude oil, which plunged 5% last night to $91.76 — that's a meaningful drop. Gold ticked up 0.35% to $4,537/oz. The Aussie dollar climbed to 71.7 US cents, up 0.22%.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Today's close — mild selloff, nothing dramatic.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session — small gain despite some tech names slipping.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Last night — big drop. OPEC cut its demand forecast for 2026, pushing oil sharply lower.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Last night — nudged higher, continues to hold elevated levels.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar rising even as RBA rate hike odds are fading — traders seem more focused on global risk appetite.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is Labor pushing ahead with a package that links new tax cuts for middle-income earners to changes in how property investors get tax breaks. The RBA rate debate is also heating up, with one expert loudly calling for hikes while markets are actually pricing in fewer rises.

stories.title: Labor ties popular tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: Labor is linking new income tax cuts — aimed at Australians earning under $135,000 — to changes in two major property investment tax perks: the CGT (capital gains tax) discount and negative gearing. Currently, if you sell an investment property you've held over 12 months, you only pay tax on half the profit (the 50% CGT discount). Labor wants to reduce that discount. Negative gearing — where you claim losses on an investment property against your regular income — would also be tightened on existing properties. If you're a property investor, this one hits you directly. The ABC reports Labor is ignoring calls to pause on these changes and is pressing ahead despite pushback.

stories.title: Labor to ignore call for pause on CGT changes
stories.why_it_matters: Despite industry calls to slow down and consult further, the Labor government is pushing full steam ahead with its CGT and negative gearing changes. This means property investors and anyone holding assets with large capital gains (like shares) should pay close attention — these changes could be moving faster than expected. No date confirmed yet, but the political momentum is clearly in one direction.

stories.title: 'Get on with it': Expert defies consensus and demands RBA hikes rates
stories.why_it_matters: One prominent economist is going against the grain and calling on the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia — the body that sets interest rates) to keep raising rates to fight inflation. But the broader market consensus has shifted the other way: traders are now betting the RBA won't hike as aggressively as previously thought. This has caused a rush of buying in Australian government bonds (essentially people lending money to the government), which drives bond prices up and yields — the interest rate the government pays — down. For you as an investor, softer rate expectations generally support growth assets like shares.

stories.title: Why is the Australian Dollar rising despite weakening RBA rate hike odds?
stories.why_it_matters: Normally, when people expect the RBA to raise rates less, the Aussie dollar falls (because higher rates attract foreign money, boosting the currency). But the AUD actually rose today to 71.7 US cents — an apparent contradiction. The likely reason is broader global risk appetite improving, with investors feeling more comfortable and buying into higher-yielding currencies like the AUD regardless of the domestic rate outlook. A stronger AUD is good news if you're buying imported goods, but it does slightly reduce the Aussie-dollar value of your US-denominated holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO).

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Google's launch of Gemini Omni — a brand new, more powerful AI model. Meanwhile, the Pope has released a major document calling for global AI regulation, warning that some autonomous weapons are already beyond meaningful human control. Both stories have real implications.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini Omni
stories.why_it_matters: Google has just announced Gemini Omni, the latest addition to its Gemini AI family. The 'Omni' branding typically signals a model that can handle text, images, audio and video all in one — so think of it as a single AI that can see, hear and read simultaneously rather than needing separate tools. This is directly relevant to your GOOGL holding: Google is staying firmly in the AI race and this announcement could be a positive catalyst when US markets open tonight, potentially helping offset yesterday's 1.2% price dip.

stories.title: Pope Leo calls for robust global AI regulation and warns autonomous weapons are ungovernable
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo has published what's being described as a manifesto on AI and humanity's future. The key warnings: some autonomous weapons systems (think AI-guided drones or missiles) have already reached a point where humans can't meaningfully intervene once they're deployed. The Pope is calling on world governments to establish binding international regulation — not voluntary guidelines — for AI development. This isn't just a moral statement; if major economies respond with legislation, it could significantly affect how companies like Google and Microsoft develop and deploy AI products. Something to watch as the regulatory conversation intensifies globally.

stories.title: Data Privacy and AI Progress — the growing tension
stories.why_it_matters: A regulatory analysis piece out today explores the fundamental tension between feeding AI models more data (which makes them smarter) and protecting individual privacy. The core issue: the better AI gets, the more data it tends to need — but stricter privacy rules limit what data companies can use. For investors in GOOGL and MSFT, this regulatory tug-of-war is a long-running background risk that could slow AI development timelines or increase compliance costs if governments tighten the rules.

sport.summary: NRL Round 13 team news is dropping with some significant injury and suspension news. AFL is mourning the death of Neale Daniher, one of the game's most beloved figures. And a World Surf League event in New Zealand was halted after an Australian photographer was bitten — possibly by a shark.

stories.title: Neale Daniher passes away — AFL mourns a giant of the game
stories.why_it_matters: Neale Daniher, the former Melbourne Demons coach and long-time Motor Neurone Disease (MND) awareness campaigner, has passed away. Daniher coached Melbourne from 1998 to 2007 and was diagnosed with MND in 2013. He became one of the most respected figures in Australian sport — not just for football but for his extraordinary courage and fundraising work, helping raise tens of millions of dollars for MND research through the Big Freeze event at the MCG. Garry Lyon and the broader AFL world are paying tribute today, and Lyon has called on PM Anthony Albanese to take action on MND funding in Daniher's honour.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 team tips: Warriors and Tigers cop major injury blows
stories.why_it_matters: Heading into Round 13, both the Warriors and Tigers have been hit hard by injury. Fox Sports reports that one Warriors hero has confirmed his season is over ('that's my footy done'), while there's also a late twist around Isaah Yeo and Origin selections creating uncertainty across multiple squads. The Tigers are also without key players. There's mystery surrounding several State of Origin stars and whether they'll feature for their clubs this weekend. Check the full team lists before locking in your NRL Fantasy lineup.

stories.title: World Surf League event halted in New Zealand after photographer bitten by 'shark or sea lion'
stories.why_it_matters: A World Surf League competition in New Zealand was put on hold after an Australian photographer was bitten while in the water. Authorities haven't confirmed whether it was a shark or a sea lion, but the WSL suspended the event as a precaution while investigations are underway. No life-threatening injuries reported, but it's a significant disruption to the contest. The incident is a reminder of the real risks for water sports professionals and will likely prompt a safety review before competition resumes.

stories.title: AFL's Lions slaughter exposes the competition's biggest structural problem
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports columnist Healy has used Brisbane Lions' recent dominant victory as a springboard to call out what he describes as a 'farce' in how AFL handles competition balance — specifically the draft and salary cap system allowing powerhouse clubs to run roughshod over the competition. The piece argues there's one remaining lever the AFL can pull to address the imbalance, though it stops short of a full fix. Good context for anyone following the competition this season.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Gemini Omni launch could reverse yesterday's dip tonight
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 1.2% last night but has just launched Gemini Omni — a powerful new multimodal AI model (meaning it can handle text, images, audio and video together). This is a meaningful product announcement that could lift sentiment when US markets open tonight around 11:30 PM AEST. Hold and watch tonight's open.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Sharp 4.4% drop — worth monitoring for a bounce
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 4.4% to $227.55 last night with no clear single catalyst in the news. GTA 6 pre-order buzz is building (collector's editions incoming), which is a medium-term positive. Unless you see further deterioration tonight, this looks like noise rather than a structural problem. Hold for now.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil down 5% — energy ETF under pressure
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil crashed 5% last night to $91.76, and OPEC just cut its global oil demand growth forecast for 2026. FUEL.AX only fell 0.9% today which is actually pretty resilient, but if oil stays weak this week there could be more downside to come. Nothing to panic about, but keep an eye on the oil price.

watch_today.title: Labor's CGT and negative gearing changes — act if you hold investment properties
watch_today.detail: Labor is pushing ahead with plans to reduce the CGT (capital gains tax) discount — currently you only pay tax on 50% of the profit from selling an asset held over 12 months — and to tighten negative gearing rules on existing properties. These changes are moving faster than expected. If you hold investment properties or are planning to sell assets with large capital gains, it's worth talking to your accountant sooner rather than later.

watch_today.title: RBA rate outlook softening — good for growth assets
watch_today.detail: Markets are increasingly pricing in fewer RBA rate hikes, which is generally a tailwind for shares and property. Your VDHG and VTS holdings benefit from a lower-rate environment. Nothing to act on today, but the macro wind is shifting in a supportive direction for your portfolio.
